decisions.statement: The reading is taken on the workstation with the checkout.
The level is kept beside the readout the level was taken for.
The session row is reached through the one module saying where a day is kept.
A session beside a day moved into akasha is read from akasha.
How to read the answer is on the readout's own page.
The open session comes from `openSession` rather than from a query written here.
A `session-tracking` row is read out of a sidecar beside a day page.
The `daily-tracking` file list names the markdown half and the akasha half.
A query for an empty end-time reaches the markdown half and the akasha half.
A session opened before its day moved and closed after is answered by two rows.
Newest-first over `start-time` does not choose between a pre-move row and a post-move row.
Choosing between a pre-move row and a post-move row belongs to `openSession`.
`levelIn` is akasha's own guard.
`levelIn` is carried unchanged.
No open session is no reading.
An open session with no level is no reading.
A level spelling no number is no reading rather than a level of zero.
`openSession` answers a row whose keys are camelized.
`levelIn` reads the spelling the store keeps.
The one key `levelIn` reads is spelled back to kebab here.
A run of this file takes a reading.
The root read is the root the environment states or the folder the call was made in.
An empty value in the environment states no root.
Where the readout's page sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
The level itself is never printed.
Importing this file takes no reading.
Nothing here decides when a reading is due.

definition: the safety level Alan logged, taken from his open block and kept on the safety readout
